stem:
The diagram shows parallelogram $ABCD$ with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meeting at $O$.

Which claim about the diagonals is correct for every parallelogram?

options.text: The diagonals are equal in length, because the figure is labelled parallelogram.
Call the answer diagonal only, with no statement about $O$, $AC$, or $BD$.
The diagonals bisect each other: $O$ is the midpoint of both $AC$ and $BD$.
Bisection holds for $AC$ even when $O$ is not the midpoint of $BD$.

teacher.key_rationale: In every parallelogram the diagonals bisect each other; equal length needs a special case (rectangle/square/rhombus constraints). The label alone does not force equal diagonals. Naming only diagonal skips the property. One-sided midpoint drops full bisection.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote parallelogram source into ABCD with diagonals at O.
